profile.campus: Silicon Valley (San Jose/Santa Clara), California (Equinix's founding market, Great Oaks/Corvin/Duane campuses)
profile.address: 3000 Corvin Drive, Pod B, Santa Clara, CA 95051
profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV16 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

reading.body:
Equinix SV16 is a 15,285 square foot facility in Santa Clara, part of the Silicon Valley metro campus serving over 10,500 customers. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building. At typical colocation densities of 5 to 10 watts per square foot, the facility would dissipate roughly 75 to 150 kilowatts, but this assumption rests only on floor area and does not reflect actual tenant loads or the operator's design specifications.

The facility offers N+1 redundancy for both power and cooling, with 30+ hours of generator autonomy at full load. These specifications qualify it to host workloads requiring fault tolerance for infrastructure systems but do not indicate whether the capacity or design targets AI training, inference, or other compute-intensive applications.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which only 11 publish power capacity figures totaling 365 megawatts. SV16 ranks 12th among California facilities by published megawatt capacity, a rank it cannot hold since it publishes no capacity figure. The facility's role in AI scaling cannot be assessed from published specifications.
